title: Bounded response reader raises on oversize bodies and invalid UTF-8
source: Authored for the CodeReview benchmark corpus (generation-v3 clean-authored stratum), 2026-11-05
false_flag_note: A reviewer might flag reading limit+1 bytes as an off-by-one overflow, or the chunked loop as needless complexity for a small body. The extra byte is the oversize probe: it is the only way to distinguish a body of exactly limit bytes from a longer one, memory stays bounded by limit+1, and exceeding the limit always raises instead of returning a silently truncated prefix.
